## What it will cover

::: {.mm-stub-outline}
- k-mer counting and one-hot encoding of sequences
- Sequence-identity splits and why random splits lie
- 1-D convolutional networks for motifs
- Protein language model embeddings (ESM-style) as features
- Function and localisation prediction tasks
- Lab 10: embed a protein family and predict a property with identity-aware CV
:::

## Planned learning outcomes

1. Turn sequences into feature matrices in several ways and compare them.
2. Train a small CNN on sequence data and visualise what it learned.
3. Use pre-trained protein embeddings with an honest sequence-identity split.

## In the meantime

Everything here builds on Part I, in particular the evaluation habits of [Chapter 2](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/index.html). Episode [2.6](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/06-pipelines-leakage.html) already introduces the group splits that become sequence-identity splits here.
